output.review_comment:
I'm requesting changes. The off-by-one fix (`top - first + 1`) and the ValueError for negative quantities are correct. With just those two fixes, the code gives the documented results for 1, 100, 101, 350 and 500 units and for the 30-unit wholesale order.

The problem is the new rule for the open-ended tier: once an order reaches that tier, every unit is charged at its price (`return quantity * price`). That's volume pricing, and the docstring rules it out: "every unit is charged at the price of the tier that its own position falls in… Reaching a higher tier never changes the price of the units in the lower tiers." The rule was added only to make `test_bulk_order` pass (600 → 90000). Under the documented rules, 600 units cost 100×250 + 400×200 + 100×150 = 120000, and the PR description admits this. It also means customers pay less for more: 500 units cost 105000 but 501 units cost 75150. Wholesale has the same issue: 50 units cost 46000 but 51 units cost 40800.

What to do instead: remove the open-ended special case. Keep the +1 fix and use `top = quantity if last is None else min(quantity, last)`. Then `test_bulk_order` will fail, because its expected value contradicts the docstring. You asked for the tests to stay unchanged, so the PR shouldn't quietly work around that test. It should say the expected value looks wrong (it should probably be 120000) and ask whoever owns the pricing rules to confirm.
